$comment: Recorded history for the ledger-provenance control (scripts/city-ledger-provenance.cjs), produced by measurement and never hand-tuned. This file exists because a control introduced into an append-only ledger with 63 existing entries has to be honest about what it finds: the entries below are the ones that predate the control or are known to violate it, and a reader can re-derive every one of them from git. It is NOT a whitelist for new entries -- an id that is not listed here is checked on every run, and adding an id here is a recorded act, not a way to make a check pass.

rules.recorded_before_containing_commit_ration: An entry's `timestamp_utc` is the moment it was WRITTEN, and it is written before the commit that carries it. Measured over the 63 historical entries, 38 fall inside [-90, +5] minutes of their containing commit, and the largest honest lead is -36 minutes (CC-009, which closed a round before its final commit). +5 minutes is the tolerance for the write-to-commit gap; anything later than that is a claim about a moment AFTER the commit that already contains it, which cannot be true.
rules.recorded_before_containing_commit_max_le: The lower bound. No historical entry legitimately precedes its commit by more than 36 minutes, so 90 minutes is the tightest round number that keeps every entry the rule is meant to keep -- a bound chosen to fit the evidence rather than the other way round.
rules.timestamp_utc_format: strict ISO-8601 UTC instant, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, and nothing else
rules.timestamp_utc_format_rationale: The field is read by automation (scripts/city-final-acceptance.cjs, this control) -- see workbook section 5, 'machine-read fields must not carry prose'. Prose belongs on the continuation line below, which this control also requires so the explanation cannot be lost while the field stays parseable.

pre_format_entries.$comment: Entries written before the entry schema was actually applied to the field. CC-019 and CC-020 carry headings and prose but no ENTRY_ID/timestamp_utc block at all, so a control that required the block would fail on history it cannot rewrite. Both are appended-only evidence and are recorded here rather than edited.
pre_format_entries.CC-019: no ENTRY_ID/timestamp_utc block: the entry is prose under a `## CC-019` heading
pre_format_entries.CC-020: no ENTRY_ID/timestamp_utc block: the entry is prose under a `## CC-020` heading

historical_violations.$comment: Entries whose recorded timestamp is LATER than the committer instant of the commit that first carried them, by more than the +5 minute tolerance. Measured with `node scripts/city-ledger-provenance.cjs --json`: 25 entries, from +7 minutes (CC-025) to +606 minutes (CC-014). These values are preserved as evidence -- the ledger is append-only and the defect is a record of what the field actually said, so it is disclosed and grandfathered, not rewritten. The mechanism is analysed in ledger CC-065.

historical_violations_note: 25 ids are listed for 26 violating ENTRIES: CC-027 appears twice in the ledger (two `## CC-027` sections under one ENTRY_ID, at lines 2041 and 2182) and only the later one violates the tolerance. The duplicate id is itself recorded here because a control that silently collapsed the two would be hiding an entry.

timestamp_hygiene_violations.$comment: Entries whose `timestamp_utc` value carries prose, a two-part shorthand without seconds, or a second time on the same line. This is the workbook section 5 defect already visible in history: 27 of 63 entries. They are preserved as-is for the same reason as above, and the continuation-line convention this control requires starts with CC-065.
